s: Forbes profile, real-time net worth as of 21 Aug 2026

why: The GPU glut after the 2018 crypto crash let them buy Nvidia cards at distressed prices while cloud incumbents were still buying CPUs. Owning depreciated silicon and cheap power contracts meant they could quote AI compute below AWS and Azure years before those firms had comparable inventory.
obst: The 2018 Ethereum collapse wiped out the mining business they had just built and forced a total pivot; the company then carried billions in GPU-backed debt at double-digit rates, and its March 2025 IPO priced at 40 dollars, below the 47-to-55 range, after investors balked at customer concentration.
turn: The 2019 decision to keep the GPUs and rent them out rather than liquidate the mining fleet.

turn: Nvidias 2023 decision to allocate H100s to CoreWeave ahead of larger clouds, which made the company the default AI capacity provider.

obst: Quantum lost its founding Commodore contract, nearly ran out of money twice before 1992, and was sued and investigated in 1996 over busy signals after flat-rate pricing overwhelmed its modems; the Time Warner merger then destroyed roughly 99 billion dollars of value and cost him the chairmanship in 2003.
turn: The 1996 switch from hourly billing to 19.95 dollars a month unlimited, which broke the metered-access model industry-wide.
